articles.title: Erie Indemnity Stock: Is ERIE Underperforming the Financial Services Sector?
articles.summary: Erie Indemnity has trailed the broader financial services sector over the past year, but Wall Street analysts remain cautiously optimistic about its outlook.
articles.body:
Erie Indemnity Company (ERIE), with a market capitalization of approximately $11 billion, is a management company serving Erie Insurance Exchange, a subscriber-owned property and casualty insurer. Based in Erie, Pennsylvania, it manages key sales, underwriting, policy issuance, and administrative functions on behalf of policyholders through the Erie Insurance Group.

Companies valued between $10 billion and $200 billion are generally classified as "large-cap stocks," and Erie Indemnity fits this description, with its market capitalization reflecting its substantial size and established position within the financial services sector. Erie Indemnity stands out for its strong financial foundation and focused insurance business model. As attorney-in-fact for Erie Insurance Exchange, it receives recurring management fee revenue, while low debt, strong cash flow, and high profitability support financial resilience and operational stability.

Despite these strengths, ERIE has slipped 27.7% from its 52-week high of $330.54, reached on October 27, 2025. Over the past three months, ERIE stock has climbed 8.1%, outperforming the State Street Financial Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLF), which has gained 4.3% during the same time frame.

Shares of ERIE have declined 16.6% year-to-date and 25.2% over the past year, trailing the ETF's 2% year-to-date gain and 3.2% increase over the same period.

ERIE shares have traded below both their 50-day and 200-day moving averages only since mid-September, signaling a recent downtrend.

Erie Indemnity has lagged the broader market over the past year, with its weaker stock performance coinciding with moderating premium growth and policy retention. The company's recent results showed slower growth in direct written premiums, while policies in force and retention also declined, pointing to a more challenging growth environment.

Still, Erie reported second-quarter results on July 30, with net income rising 3.2% year over year to $180.3 million, or $3.45 per share, while revenue increased 2.8% to $1.09 billion. The results highlighted continued earnings resilience despite slower growth trends. Erie shares subsequently jumped 3.6% in the following trading session, suggesting a positive market reaction to the quarterly results.

articles.title: How Is United Airlines' Stock Performance Compared to Other Global Jets Stocks?
articles.summary: United Airlines has underperformed the Global Jets industry over the past year, but analysts are highly optimistic about the stock’s prospects.
articles.body:
Chicago, Illinois-based United Airlines Holdings, Inc. (UAL) owns and manages airlines that transports people and cargos serving customers worldwide. With a market cap of $35.3 billion, the company also offers catering, ground handling, flight academy, and maintenance services for third parties.

Companies worth $10 billion or more are generally described as "large-cap stocks," and UAL perfectly fits that description, with its market cap exceeding this mark, underscoring its size, influence, and dominance within the airlines industry. UAL's extensive route network, strategic hubs, and loyalty program drive its competitive edge in global aviation, facilitating high-volume international and long-haul flights.

Despite its notable strength, UAL slipped 21.7% from its 52-week high of $138.77, achieved on Jun. 30. Over the past three months, UAL stock has declined 8.1%, outperforming the U.S. Global Jets ETF's (JETS) 9% dip during the same time frame.

In the longer term, shares of UAL fell 2.8% on a YTD basis but climbed 3.2% over the past 52 weeks, underperforming JETS' YTD marginal gains and 8.9% returns during the same time frame.

To confirm the bearish trend, UAL has been trading below its 50-day moving average since mid-August. The stock is trading below its 200-day moving average since late August, with some fluctuations.

UAL stock performance has been primarily constrained by macroeconomic and industry-wide headwinds that overshadowed solid operational delivery. The foremost driver of investor hesitation has been persistent energy volatility, surging global crude oil prices significantly inflated jet fuel expenses, adding roughly $2.3 billion in quarterly fuel costs in 2026, which squeezed net profit margins despite high passenger demand. Additionally, investor sentiment across the broader airline sector was dampened by elevated interest rates. External factors such as broader market sell-offs driven by rising Treasury yields and systemic uncertainties surrounding U.S. air traffic control funding and capacity adjustments also frequently triggered short-term pullbacks, keeping the shares from fully tracking the company's strong revenue growth and earnings beats.

articles.title: Trafigura Launches Volare Shipping to Cash In on Record Tanker Rates
articles.summary: Trafigura is spinning off its supertanker fleet into Volare Shipping, targeting an Oslo listing as Hormuz-driven freight rates hit record highs.
articles.body:
One of the world's biggest oil traders, Trafigura, is spinning off its supertanker business in a new company.

Trafigura on Monday said it had established a new, dedicated group company, Volare Shipping Ltd, to own, operate, and scale a modern fleet of oil tankers. The fleet will be commercially managed by Trafigura's global shipping business.

Volare Shipping currently operates six very large crude carriers (VLCCs) and has eight newbuild vessels on order, scheduled to be delivered between 2026 and 2028.

Volare Shipping has also said that it considers a private placement to raise about $500 million and a subsequent proposed listing of the company's shares on the Euronext Growth Oslo stock exchange.

Following the proposed listing, Trafigura will be the majority owner of Volare Shipping, the commodity trading giant said.

Subject to a listing approval and a successful completion of the private placement, Volare Shipping's shares are expected to start trading on Euronext Growth Oslo on or about October 5, 2026, under the ticker VLCC.

Trafigura says it currently manages about 500 vessels across multiple segments, including around 250 oil tankers.

"Long-term fundamentals in crude oil transportation remain supportive, and a dedicated, listed company gives Volare Shipping investors direct exposure to the sector," said Andrea Olivi, Global Head of Shipping at Trafigura and Chair of the Board of Directors of Volare Shipping.

"Oslo is home to one of the world's leading stock exchanges for shipping companies," Olivi added.

According to Alexandre Duff, Chief Executive Officer of Volare Shipping, "The contemplated private placement will fully fund our current newbuilding programme, while our proven operational expertise positions Volare Shipping to deliver attractive long-term value for all shareholders."

Trafigura's new venture into the tanker market comes as the Strait of Hormuz crisis has pushed oil tanker freight rates to record highs.

The daily rate to charter a tanker has recently topped $1 million for the first time ever, amid tightening supply of vessels to carry crude oil and fuels, and owners' reluctance to risk passage through the Strait of Hormuz.

Technology became the strategy's largest overweight at 17%, largely because index reconstitution sharply reduced the benchmark's technology allocation. Looking ahead to 2026, the outlook for small-cap equities remains constructive due to improving monetary conditions and attractive valuations, despite a lack of anticipated rotation toward higher-quality businesses. The firm remains committed to disciplined, quality-focused investing; historically, quality prevails over the long term. articles.title: Priority Technology Holdings going private in $1.6 billion deal
articles.summary: An investor group led by Chairman and CEO Thomas Priore will pay $8.05 per share, a 65% premium to the company's unaffected share price
articles.body:
Thomas Priore, the Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Priority Technology Holdings, is leading an investor group that will take the company private in a transaction valued at approximately $1.6 billion in enterprise value, the company announced Monday.

The investor group has agreed to purchase every Priority Technology Holdings share it does not currently hold for $8.05 per share in cash. That price represents a 65% premium to the company's closing price on Nov. 7, 2025, the last trading day before the group's preliminary acquisition proposal became public, and a 38% premium to the company's closing price on Sept. 18, 2026, the last trading day before Monday's announcement.

The special committee, composed solely of independent directors with no conflicting interests, gave the transaction its unanimous blessing following an evaluation that encompassed a valuation analysis and arm's-length negotiations with Priore and his affiliates. Through those talks, the committee secured a final offer that was more than 30% above what had originally been put on the table. The full board approved the transaction based on the committee's recommendation.

"After a comprehensive evaluation of the proposal, a rigorous valuation analysis, and extensive negotiations with Tom and his affiliates, we are delivering a transaction that provides compelling and certain value to Priority's unaffiliated stockholders," Special Committee Chair Michael Passilla said in a statement.

The deal is being financed in part by equity commitments from funds advised by Searchlight Capital Partners, and is not subject to any financing conditions, the company said. Searchlight is a global private investment firm with $17 billion in assets under management.

In a Schedule 13D filing in December 2025, Priore had informed the special committee that he has no plans to sell his shares in the company to an outside buyer, the company said.

The transaction is subject to customary closing conditions, including regulatory approvals and approval by holders of a majority of Priority Technology Holdings stock not affiliated with the investor group. The deal is expected to close in the first half of 2027. Upon completion, Priority Technology Holdings stock will be delisted from the Nasdaq Global Select Market.

Barclays is serving as financial advisor to the special committee, with Paul, Weiss, Rifkind, Wharton & Garrison LLP as its legal counsel. TD Securities is serving as placement agent to the investor group, with McDermott Will & Schulte LLP as legal counsel. Latham & Watkins LLP is serving as legal counsel to Searchlight.

articles.title: Barilla to shake-up domestic pasta production
articles.summary: The Italy-based group said the moves would help the company “stay competitive in a challenging market”.
articles.body:
Barilla is in talks to sell three production sites in Italy as part of plans to revamp its manufacturing in the south of the country.

The Italy-based group said the moves would help the company "stay competitive in a challenging market".

Family-owned Barilla, one of the world's largest pasta manufacturers, is in talks to sell a factory in Marcianise to local rival Pastificio Liguori.

The business is also in negotiations to sell mills in Ancona and Bari to Italian miller Molino Casillo.

Barilla described the discussions as "advanced".

The company is planning to create a "new pasta production hub" in the city of Foggia. Barilla plans to invest €100m ($114.8m) to build a mill to support the existing pasta plant.

In a statement, the group said the move, scheduled to be completed in 2030, would "deliver significant improvements in sustainability, logistics and production efficiency to serve both domestic and international markets".

Barilla said the project would create jobs but did not disclose details. Just Food has approached the company for more information on the investment.

"This move addresses the need to improve our logistics and production efficiency – an essential factor for remaining competitive in the challenging pasta market," Giovanni Palopoli, head of operations for pasta solutions at Barilla, said in the statement.

The company's revenues fell slightly in 2025, landing at €4.83bn, compared to €4.88bn a year earlier. Pasta accounted for more than 46% of sales.

In Barilla's annual report for 2025, the company said pressure on household income had led to "aggressive price competition", which had "led to the need for rapid adjustments aimed at streamlining operations".

Nevertheless, Barilla's pre-tax profits increased 25% to €342m. The group's consolidated profit for the year was €233m, an increase of more than 64% on 12 months earlier.

The annual report showed Barilla had a combined 15 plants and mills in Italy last year. It also has 15 production sites overseas, including in North America, Europe and Russia.

In May, Barilla set out plans to expand a factory in New York state to "meet growing demand" in the US .

articles.title: Interview: Revolut chief banking officer Sid Jajodia on growth, margins and  IPO plans
articles.summary: Sid Jajodia tells Vidhya Edwards how generating 76% of turnover from fees protects the bank's 38% pre-tax margin from interest-rate cuts.
articles.body:
Revolut is scaling its global banking business while seeking to maintain strong profitability and reduce its exposure to interest-rate cycles. The company is targeting 100 million customers by 2027, supported by new market launches and a growing range of financial products.

In this interview, Sid Jajodia, Revolut's chief banking officer , tells Retail Banker International (RBI) the company's expansion strategy, diversified revenue base, plans to provide Finnish account numbers, and its decision to focus on growth rather than comment on IPO timing.

RBI: You've set a goal to hit 100 million customers by 2027. Where is that next massive wave of users coming from?

Sid Jajodia : Customer acquisition momentum remains strong, backed by our rapidly expanding global footprint as well as our growing product suite. In January 2026, Revolut launched its first bank outside of Europe in Mexico and since then we've also launched our bank in Australia. Meanwhile, we've been strengthening our position in existing markets, such as the UK and France, by securing full banking licences.

We've also continued to roll out features that drive deeper customer engagement including paid plans and RevPoints across our 40+ markets. As such, we remain firmly on track to reach 100 million customers by 2027.

RBI: You're investing $13bn to expand globally. To speed things up, are you planning strategic acquisitions of local banks, or will this growth be purely organic?

Sid Jajodia : Revolut continuously explores all growth opportunities to bring the Revolut app to customers worldwide.

Driven by our ambition to serve over 100 million daily active customers across 100 countries, we continue to execute ambitious expansion strategies - highlighted by recent licensing milestones across high-growth markets such as Mexico, France, Australia, Colombia, Peru and the UAE.

RBI: A 38% pre-tax profit margin is incredible for banking. As central bank interest rates start coming down globally and squeeze interest income, how do you protect that Profitability?

Sid Jajodia : Revolut has a robust and diversified business model where fee based revenue - spanning subscriptions, card payments, wealth and FX - accounts for 76% of turnover, leaving only 21% directly exposed to interest rate fluctuations.

In 2025, 11 distinct product lines within Revolut generated over £100 million ($135 million) in annual revenue, with no single stream accounting for more than 22% of group income. We pride ourselves on this revenue diversification which continues to drive strong top-line momentum while also making the business as a whole more resilient to external cycles.

articles.title: Crude Oil Three Rallies Before the Fall
articles.summary: The EPA changes the gasoline equation every fall. What happens next can matter to crude oil traders.
articles.body:
Each year, the U.S. gasoline market goes through an important seasonal transition. The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) generally requires lower-volatility gasoline during the summer ozone season, beginning May 1 for refiners and terminals and June 1 for retailers, and generally ending September 15. Lower Reid Vapor Pressure (RVP) gasoline reduces evaporative emissions during hot weather but can be more costly to produce. When these restrictions end, refiners transition toward winter-grade gasoline. At the same time, the peak summer driving season is ending, reducing seasonal gasoline demand and some of the demand for crude oil used by refiners.

These changes help create seasonal headwinds for crude oil during the fourth quarter. Summer vacations end, children return to school, and highway travel typically retreats from its summer peak. Another interesting influence appears late in the year. December 31 is an important property-tax assessment date for crude oil inventories in many Gulf Coast jurisdictions, giving refiners and other crude oil holders an incentive to reduce year-end stocks. U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA) data show this pattern remains remarkably persistent: from 2012 through 2025, Gulf Coast commercial crude inventories declined from November to December in 13 of 14 years, averaging about 8.9 million barrels.

This year, however, seasonality must share the stage with geopolitical risk in the Middle East. The region remains critical to global petroleum supplies, and unexpected military escalation, production disruption, or interference with major shipping routes could quickly alter the supply-and-demand outlook. That does not eliminate the historical fourth-quarter tendency toward weaker crude oil prices, but it reminds traders that seasonality is a tendency—not a guarantee. The seasonal setup may favor the short side. However, traders still need a defined risk-management plan that can protect them when an unexpected geopolitical event produces a sharp counter-seasonal rally.

articles.title: Dólar opera em alta, de olho em ata do Copom e Lula na ONU; Ibovespa cai | G1
articles.standfirst: Na véspera, a moeda americana recuou 0,70%, cotada a R$ 5,1082. Já a bolsa brasileira avançou 0,74%, aos 186.596 pontos.
articles.summary: Na véspera, a moeda americana recuou 0,70%, cotada a R$ 5,1082. Já a bolsa brasileira avançou 0,74%, aos 186.596 pontos.
articles.body:
O dólar opera em alta nesta terça-feira (22), com um avanço de 0,06% perto das 12h, cotado a R$ 5,1115 . Já o Ibovespa , principal índice da bolsa brasileira, tinha queda de 0,36% no mesmo horário, aos 185.929 pontos .

O destaque da sessão fica com a ata da última reunião de juros do Comitê de Política Monetária (Copom). Investidores também acompanham a queda nos preços do petróleo, que pode pressionar ações do setor de energia, e o discurso do presidente Lula (PT) na Organização das Nações Unidas (ONU).

▶️A ata da última reunião do Copom fica no centro das atenções nesta terça-feira. No documento, o Banco Central (BC) reconheceu a desaceleração da atividade econômica, do crédito e da inflação, mas ponderou os riscos fiscais e a incerteza quanto ao cenário internacional. No último boletim Focus, divulgado ontem, a projeção dos economistas é que a Selic termine 2026 em 13,5% ao ano.

▶️ O discurso de Lula na ONU também fica no radar. As falas acontecem em meio a um momento delicado entre Brasil e Estados Unidos , que continuam sem avanço nas negociações das tarifas americanas sobre produtos brasileiros.

▶️ Investidores continuam a monitorar a queda nos preços do petróleo. No final de semana, a China atendeu a um pedido da Arábia Saudita e pediu que o Irã limitasse os ataques dos rebeldes houthis à infraestrutura petrolífera do país.

Perto das 12h, o barril do Brent , referência internacional, tinha queda de 0,36% , cotado a US$ 99,98 . Já o West Texas Intermediate ( WTI ), referência nos EUA, caía 0,47% , a US$ 95,33 o barril.

▶️ Ainda no exterior, o mercado também segue em compasso de espera pela cúpula entre Trump e Xi Jinping , prevista para quinta-feira. A expectativa é que os líderes sinalizem uma prorrogação da trégua comercial firmada entre os dois países no ano passado e que evitou um grande choque na economia global. Questões envolvendo Taiwan também podem ser abordadas.

Veja abaixo mais detalhes do dia no mercado.

As tensões no Oriente Médio seguem no radar dos investidores. De um lado, o crescente conflito entre os EUA e o Irã continuam a diminuir as esperanças de que o Estreito de Ormuz — rota por onde passava cerca de 20% de todo o comércio global de petróleo antes da guerra na região — seja reaberto em breve.

No domingo (20), o presidente americano, Donald Trump , afirmou que estava decidindo se "explodiria o Irã inteiro ou não" . A declaração foi dada à emissora americana Fox News, e ocorre em meio a temores de que os EUA retomem os bombardeios em larga escala contra o país do Oriente Médio.

Ainda assim, a sinalização da Arábia Saudita, na semana passada, de que ofereceria cargas adicionais de petróleo por rotas alternativas, trouxe alívio aos preços da commodity nos últimos dias.

No sábado, a China atendeu a um pedido do país e solicitou ao Irã que limitasse os ataques dos rebeldes houthis à infraestrutura petrolífera saudita, que têm ameaçado uma segunda rota de exportação de petróleo no Oriente Médio.

A Arábia Saudita também informou, na semana passada, que buscava restaurar cerca de metade da capacidade de seu oleoduto Leste-Oeste, após a interrupção sofrida devido a ataques de drones. A notícia também ajudou a diminuir preocupações com a oferta global de petróleo e ajudava a reduzir os preços da commodity.

Os mercados financeiros também seguem na expectativa pela cúpula entre os presidentes Donald Trump e Xi Jinping , prevista para quinta-feira.

Além da prorrogação do acordo comercial, os dois países também devem tratar sobre inteligência artificial.

Estados Unidos e China consideram os avanços na tecnologia estratégicos para a competitividade econômica e militar dos dois países. Washington e Pequim, no entanto, mantêm divergências importantes sobre o setor.

Entre os principais pontos de atrito estão as restrições americanas ao acesso da China a chips avançados, acusações envolvendo cópia e transferência de tecnologia e diferenças sobre como a indústria de inteligência artificial deve ser regulada.

Os Estados Unidos têm restringido o acesso chinês a semicondutores de ponta e outras tecnologias consideradas estratégicas, enquanto a China critica as medidas e acusa Washington de tentar limitar seu desenvolvimento tecnológico.

Em Wall Street , os principais índices americanos operavam mistos, com investidores de olho em Trump na ONU e em meio às expectativas de negociações no Oriente Médio.

Perto das 12h, o Dow Jones caía 0,44%, enquanto o S&P 500 subia 0,01% e o Nasdaq Composite tinha alta de 0,38%.

Na Europa , a maioria das bolsas locais operava em alta, também de olho no petróleo. No mesmo horário, o DAX , da Alemanha, subia 0,05%, enquanto o CAC-40 , da França, avançava 0,25%. O FTSE 100 , do Reino Unido, ia na contramão e tinha queda de 0,19%

Na Ásia , a maioria dos mercados acionários fecharam em alta modesta, em meio à expectativa de que a China e os EUA prorroguem a trégua comercial na reunião entre Trump e Xi Jinping, prevista para quinta-feira.

O SSEC , índice de Xangai e o CSI300 , que reúne as maiores empresas das bolsas de Xangai e Shenzhen, subiram 0,1%. Já o Hang Seng, de Hong Kong , avançou 0,2%.

Entre os demais mercados da região, o Kospi , da Coreia do Sul, valorizou 0,15%, enquanto o Nikkei , do Japão, permaneceu fechado.

articles.title: Fazenda reduz previsão de crescimento da economia para 2% e cita alta do peso das dívidas das famílias | G1
articles.standfirst: Ministério também revisou para baixo a projeção de inflação para 2026, citando resultados recentes do IPCA e melhora das expectativas inflacionárias.
articles.summary: Ministério também revisou para baixo a projeção de inflação para 2026, citando resultados recentes do IPCA e melhora das expectativas inflacionárias.
articles.body:
O Ministério da Fazenda revisou para baixo a projeção de crescimento da economia brasileira neste ano, de 2,3% para 2,0%, refletindo principalmente a desaceleração do setor de serviços, influenciada pelo comprometimento da renda das famílias com o pagamento de dívidas.

"A projeção para o setor de serviços caiu de 2,4% para 1,8% e a da indústria, de 2,1% para 1,7%, movimentos parcialmente compensados pela agropecuária, revisada de 1,8% para 2,8%. Nos serviços, a revisão decorre do carrego mais fraco deixado pelo primeiro semestre e da transmissão defasada da política monetária sobre a demanda doméstica", explica o governo no Boletim Macrofiscal, divulgado nesta terça-feira (22).

A publicação, divulgada bimestralmente, reúne projeções de curto e médio prazo para indicadores de atividade econômica e inflação utilizados no processo orçamentário da União.

"Ainda que o endividamento das famílias siga estável em proporção da renda, o comprometimento com o serviço da dívida atingiu o maior nível da série histórica no segundo trimestre, o que limita a conversão do avanço da massa de rendimentos em consumo", explica o ministério.

A pasta menciona ainda o desempenho da indústria, pressionada pelo custo do crédito e pela demanda mais fraca por bens de consumo, enquanto a atividade extrativa continua sustentando o setor.

Em sentido contrário, o mercado de trabalho segue amparando os segmentos ligados ao consumo das famílias, e a ampliação da faixa de isenção do Imposto de Renda da Pessoa Física eleva a renda disponível ao longo do segundo semestre, atenuando a desaceleração projetada.

As estimativas para a inflação em 2026 também foram revistas para baixo, passando de 5,1% para 4,9%.

🔎Desde o início de 2025, com a adoção do sistema de meta contínua, o objetivo é manter a inflação em 3%, sendo considerada dentro da meta se variar entre 1,50% e 4,50%.

Entre os fatores para a revisão, o ministério cita os resultados do Índice Nacional de Preços ao Consumidor Amplo (IPCA) de julho, que ficaram abaixo do projetado anteriormente, especialmente no grupo de alimentação no domicílio e, em menor medida, no de serviços.

"A revisão também incorpora a melhora das expectativas de inflação para 2026, a manutenção da taxa Selic em patamar contracionista ao longo do ano e a desaceleração esperada da atividade econômica no segundo semestre de 2026", acrescenta o documento.

Por outro lado, a projeção incorpora fatores de pressão inflacionária, como o fenômeno El Niño. A estimativa, porém, ainda não considera as medidas recentes relacionadas aos combustíveis.

No caso da gasolina, as alíquotas do PIS/Pasep e da Cofins foram reduzidas em R$ 0,63 por litro, em substituição à subvenção de R$ 0,44 por litro. Para o etanol hidratado, as duas contribuições foram zeradas, resultando em uma redução da carga tributária de R$ 0,19 por litro.

Segundo o ministério, a desoneração da gasolina e do etanol hidratado, sem considerar a subvenção ao diesel, tem potencial para reduzir o IPCA em aproximadamente 0,15 ponto percentual.

Economia brasileira. — Foto: Jornal Nacional/ Reprodução

Já para 2027, a projeção de crescimento da economia foi revisada de 2,5% para 2,3%, refletindo os efeitos da política monetária contracionista.

"O resultado apoia-se sobretudo nos efeitos defasados do ciclo de flexibilização monetária e na continuidade da expansão da indústria extrativa e das exportações associadas. A queda da Selic iniciada em 2026 transmite-se gradualmente ao crédito e à demanda doméstica, estimulando a indústria de transformação, a construção e os serviços mais cíclicos, segmentos mais sensíveis ao ciclo de juros."

A projeção para a inflação, por sua vez, foi revisada para cima, de 3,6% para 3,8%, refletindo os efeitos de um El Niño mais intenso sobre a safra do próximo ano.

"Além dos efeitos de segunda ordem do El Niño sobre as carnes, a possível reversão do ciclo pecuário, com maior retenção de fêmeas, gera um risco ainda maior de elevação dos preços desse item. Adicionalmente, foram incorporados ao cenário a recente aceleração do IPA-DI agropecuário, que aumenta o risco de repasse dos preços do atacado ao consumidor, além dos riscos associados ao choque de fertilizantes sobre a safra de 2027, decorrentes da intensificação do conflito no Oriente Médio. Para os anos seguintes, projeta-se a convergência da inflação para a meta", explica o ministério.

Em relação ao conflito entre Estados Unidos e Irã, o governo avalia que o choque deixou de ser pontual e passou a operar como condição persistente do cenário de energia.

Isso porque o acordo provisório não evoluiu para um acordo formal e o fluxo de embarcações pelo Estreito de Ormuz permaneceu abaixo dos níveis anteriores ao conflito, ao mesmo tempo em que ataques no Mar Vermelho mantêm riscos sobre o estreito de Bab el-Mandeb.

Nesse cenário, a cotação para o petróleo Brent apresentou volatilidade expressiva, ultrapassando o patamar de U$100 por barril na primeira semana de setembro, em um momento em que os estoques mundiais têm se reduzido.

Esse é um dos motivos pelos quais a projeção para o preço médio do barril passou de US$ 79,2 para US$ 87,7 por barril, neste ano. Para 2027, também houve elevação, passando de US$ 71,0 para US$ 79,5.

articles.title: Petrobras vai perfurar 3 novos poços na Foz do Amazonas a partir de janeiro | G1
articles.standfirst: Estatal recebeu autorização do Ibama e usará os novos poços para avaliar se a descoberta de petróleo na região tem viabilidade comercial.
articles.summary: Estatal recebeu autorização do Ibama e usará os novos poços para avaliar se a descoberta de petróleo na região tem viabilidade comercial.
articles.body:
A Petrobras enviará, em janeiro, uma sonda de perfuração para a Bacia da Foz do Amazonas, no litoral do Amapá, para iniciar os trabalhos em três novos poços.

A informação foi dada nesta terça-feira (22) pela diretora de Engenharia, Tecnologia e Inovação da estatal, Renata Baruzzi, em entrevista à Reuters.

A empresa recebeu recentemente autorização do Instituto Brasileiro do Meio Ambiente e dos Recursos Naturais Renováveis ( Ibama ) para realizar as perfurações. Os poços serão usados para avaliar a viabilidade comercial da descoberta de petróleo na região.

🔎 O anúncio faz parte de um plano apresentado em agosto deste ano, que prevê investimentos de US$ 2,5 bilhões na perfuração de 15 poços na Margem Equatorial. Três desses poços aguardavam licenciamento ambiental para o início das atividades.

Margem Equatorial onde está localizada a Bacia Foz do Amazonas — Foto: Petrobras/divulgação

Petrobras vai investir US$ 2,5 bi até 2030

A Petrobras informou que o Plano de Negócios 2026-2030 prevê investimentos de US$ 2,5 bilhões (cerca de R$ 12,85 bilhões), na perfuração de 15 poços na Margem Equatorial , região considerada promissora para a expansão da produção de petróleo e gás no país.

Segundo a estatal, o valor corresponde a 37,5% do total destinado à exploração no período . Três poços aguardam licenciamento ambiental para início das atividades.

Os motivos do Ibama ter segurado as licenças até agora

O Ibama atua com cautela diante da complexidade da região e exige estudos mais detalhados antes de liberar as licenças.

Entidades como o Greenpeace e a WWF-Brasil alertam para os riscos ao Grande Sistema de Recifes da Amazônia, um ecossistema raro formado por corais e esponjas, e à extensa faixa de manguezais contínuos no litoral do Amapá.

Líderes locais e ambientalistas também destacam os possíveis impactos sobre comunidades tradicionais. Acidentes ou até mesmo a poluição sonora das embarcações podem comprometer a pesca artesanal, além de afetar territórios quilombolas e terras indígenas costeiras.

“Nós temos calendários tradicionais que são norteados a partir da mudança do tempo. Quando é período de chuva, é um período de determinadas espécies de que a gente se alimenta. Quando é verão, são outras espécies, como aves, como peixes, que vêm da água salgada também, porque o nosso território é banhado pelas águas do oceano”, disse Luene Karipuna, membro da Articulação dos Povos e Organizações Indígenas do Amapá e Norte do Pará (APOIANP).

O projeto da Petrobras na costa do Amapá é considerado estratégico para a soberania energética do país , mas também desperta preocupações sobre a preservação de ecossistemas únicos e a proteção de populações que dependem diretamente dos recursos naturais da região.

articles.title: Paramount’s $49 Billion Debt Sale to Kick Off After Lawsuits End
articles.summary: Bankers are reaching out to investors ahead of the sale of $49 billion in financing backing Paramount Skydance Corp.’s takeover of Warner Bros. Discovery Inc...
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- Bankers are reaching out to investors ahead of the sale of $49 billion in financing backing Paramount Skydance Corp.'s takeover of Warner Bros. Discovery Inc., after the company settled a series of lawsuits that had held up the $110 billion acquisition.

Bank of America Corp., Citigroup Inc., and Apollo Global Management Inc. underwrote one of the largest buyout debt packages on record earlier this year to fund the takeover, and lined up significant investor demand before the deal ground to a halt amid the threat of legal proceedings. With the takeover now cleared to close, bankers plan to start selling the debt in coming weeks, said people familiar with the matter, speaking on condition of anonymity.

The package includes about $30 billion of investment-grade bonds, $7.5 billion of investment-grade loans and roughly $12 billion of second-lien bonds, targeting a wider range of dollar and euro investors than is typical for a leveraged buyout. Borrowers rarely sell a combination of high grade and junk debt.

The debt was structured to leave Paramount on the hook, rather than its lenders, if borrowing costs rise. That should prevent a repeat of the hit banks took on so-called hung loans in 2022. Back then, a sharp rise in interest rates meant Wall Street lenders struggled to sell down the debt they'd underwritten, forcing them to hold it on their balance sheets, often at a huge loss.

The financing on the Paramount deal, however, comes with no caps on the interest rate, letting lenders raise the cost to the company if the market deteriorates, which it has done since the deal was underwritten. Both the Federal Reserve and the European Central Bank have since raised rates, and corporate credit spreads have widened.

Representatives for Warner Bros., Paramount, Apollo, Bank of America and Citigroup didn't immediately respond to requests for comment.

The expectation is that the deal will sell down quickly once it's launched, the people said. The package will be sold using financial metrics from earlier in the year, meaning the financing needs to come to market before those numbers go out of date, they added.

Regulators in nearly 70 jurisdictions have already approved the merger, and the Federal Communications Commission and other federal agencies signed off on an extraordinary level of foreign financing, making it likely the acquisition can close very soon.

articles.title: Trump Administration to Remove 750,000 From Obamacare Rolls
articles.summary: Vice President JD Vance announced the Trump administration will take hundreds of thousands of people off Obamacare plans, alleging they were improperly enrol...
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- Vice President JD Vance announced the Trump administration will take hundreds of thousands of people off Obamacare plans, alleging they were improperly enrolled.

The administration is also suspending some brokers who sell Affordable Care Act coverage, accusing them of being responsible for thousands of fraudulent enrollees, including some who didn't exist. Vance said Tuesday that the administration believes around 750,000 "are fraudulently enrolled" and added that officials would conduct "additional verification" on roughly 419,000 people.

"These programs they are deserving, they're important, but they're not going to exist unless we stop the fraud," Vance said during a press conference in the White House complex. "We are actually making sure that people receiving Obamacare subsidies are actually entitled to receive them. Amazingly we weren't doing that before."

Vance estimated the move would save $2.2 billion in taxpayer funds. The figure couldn't be immediately verified.

Shares of health insurance companies fell Tuesday morning after early news reports of the cuts. Centene Corp. fell as much as 3.9%, Molina Healthcare Inc. was down as much as 3.5%, Elevance Health Inc fell as much as 1.9%, and UnitedHealth Group Inc. was down as much as 1.4%.

Conservatives have long alleged that the Affordable Care Act markets are rife with fraud, accusations that opponents have called a smokescreen for kicking people off the program. The Trump administration has curbed some policies that made enrollment easier.

Enrollment in Obamacare markets has dropped by millions since Republicans in Congress let Covid-era subsidies expire, causing premium payments to jump for many enrollees.

Enrollment for the federal Obamacare marketplace opens Nov. 1. People shopping for plans are likely to see spikes in premiums ahead of enrollment, adding to mounting concerns about affordability ahead of the midterm elections.

articles.title: Apple Developing New Fitness Tracker Aimed at Rivaling Whoop
articles.summary: Apple Inc. is developing a screenless health and fitness tracker similar to Whoop Inc.’s wrist-worn device, part of an effort to rethink its smartwatch lineu...
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- Apple Inc. is developing a screenless health and fitness tracker similar to Whoop Inc.'s wrist-worn device, part of an effort to rethink its smartwatch lineup and add new wearable technologies.

The company has been exploring the category for several months and is now developing prototypes, according to people with knowledge of the matter. The effort has support from top executives, but Apple hasn't decided whether to release the product, said the people, who asked not to be identified because the work is confidential.

The project remains in a preliminary phase known internally as a technology investigation. If Apple proceeds with a release, the device likely won't debut before 2028. A spokesperson for the Cupertino, California-based company declined to comment.

Shares of Garmin Ltd., a seller of fitness bands, fell as much as 2.5% to a session low after Bloomberg reported on the plan. Apple was up about 1% at $342.29 as of 12:26 p.m. in New York trading.

The prototypes feature a thin fabric band with a sensor-equipped computing module. The absence of a screen would distinguish the device from the Apple Watch, a display-centric product that combines fitness tracking with apps, notifications and other functions.

The potential Whoop rival has drawn particular interest from Apple Executive Chairman Tim Cook and services chief Eddy Cue, the people said. The latter executive took over the company's health efforts late last year.

Though Apple remains a top seller of smartwatches — especially in the US — competitors such as Whoop and smart ring maker Oura Inc. are growing quickly, with millions of users each. Their rise is prompting Apple to reconsider its approach to health and fitness tracking.

At the same time, a leadership transition is underway at Apple's watch and health businesses. Jeff Williams, the former chief operating officer who oversaw both areas, retired at the end of last year. What credit score is needed for a balance transfer credit card?

A debt management plan, or DMP, is a structured repayment plan typically arranged through a nonprofit credit counseling agency. A credit counselor may work with your creditors to reduce interest rates or fees and establish a repayment schedule.

Debt management plans are primarily used for unsecured debts, such as credit cards, and can be useful if you want additional structure and professional help managing your repayment plan.

A debt consolidation loan allows you to use a personal loan to pay off multiple credit card balances, leaving you with one installment loan and one monthly payment.

Debt avalanche: Make extra payments toward the debt with the highest interest rate first while continuing to make the required payments on your other accounts. Once that debt is paid off, put the extra money toward the balance with the next-highest rate.

Debt snowball: Make extra payments toward your smallest balance first. After paying it off, roll that payment into the next-smallest balance. This approach prioritizes making visible progress rather than minimizing interest costs.

articles.title: Republican Calls for Diesel Export Ban Grow Ahead of Midterms
articles.summary: A growing number of Republican lawmakers are calling for a ban on diesel exports as the key fuel hits record prices less than two months before the midterms...
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- A growing number of Republican lawmakers are calling for a ban on diesel exports as the key fuel hits record prices less than two months before the midterms in which the GOP potentially faces steep electoral losses.

Alaska Senator Dan Sullivan, who trailed Democratic challenger Mary Peltola in the first round of voting and is one of the GOP's most endangered incumbents, was the latest to urge the move Tuesday.

Alaska relies heavily on diesel and closely related heating oil. Many remote communities depend on diesel generators for electricity. The climate is harsh, freight moves over long distances and per-capita usage of diesel and home heating oil is more than four times the national average.

US retail diesel prices have climbed above $6.50 a gallon for the first time, hammering farmers across the Grain Belt as they prepare for harvest and truckers across the country.

As prices have risen, more Republicans have embraced the idea of a diesel export ban or even price controls.

Senator Chuck Grassley, the senior Republican senator, repeatedly urged President Donald Trump in social media posts over the weekend to block diesel exports in an effort to cut prices he said were hurting farmers in Iowa.

Sullivan said he favored a diesel export ban until the Iran war is resolved.

"American fuel should stay home with Americans," Sullivan said. "The cost of diesel is just too damn high."

Sullivan said the best way to cut prices is to "produce more energy in Alaska, by Alaskans, for Alaskans."

The rising diesel prices have benefited refiners and their stock prices. Valero Energy Corp., Marathon Petroleum Corp. and Phillips 66 have all seen quarterly earnings per share almost quadruple year-over-year.

But mounting Republican support for an export ban led Jefferies to downgrade Valero and Marathon to hold from buy on Tuesday.

Other embattled Republican Senate candidates who have embraced the idea are former Representative Mike Rogers in Michigan and Representative Ashley Hinson in Iowa. Days earlier, Hinson's opponent, Democrat Josh Turek, called for a diesel export ban as part of his own plan for bringing down diesel prices.

Last week, Senate Majority Leader John Thune told reporters he was open to exploring the idea.

articles.title: GCCs shift towards mid-career AI talent, leaner teams
articles.summary: India Business News: India GCCs are shifting to lean AI-enabled pods, hiring more mid-career talent and fewer juniors, with AI skills premiums and value growth decoupled from headcount.
articles.body: Bengaluru: India’s global capability centres (GCCs) are shifting from the traditional model of large teams of junior engineers to leaner engineering pods, with three to five professionals supported by 50–100 AI agents, according to an ANSR and T500 Research report.The traditional GCC workforce has typically followed a pyramid structure, with a broad base of junior engineers supporting a smaller layer of senior architects and leaders. The emerging model is expected to have a narrower entry-level base, a larger concentration of mid-level AI-enabled engineers and a stronger leadership layer.Rather than scaling through proportional headcount growth, GCCs are expected to increasingly rely on AI-enabled execution, with employees focusing on AI orchestration, solution architecture, validation, governance and complex business problem-solving. Hiring is also shifting from individual roles to outcome-oriented pods and multidisciplinary squads that can be deployed rapidly for product development, AI adoption and business transformation.The report describes this as “Workforce 2.0”, in which the unit of workforce planning shifts from the employee seat to the capability. The traditional pyramid gives way to a diamond-shaped structure, with greater talent density in mid- to senior-level problem-solving roles. Success is increasingly measured by enterprise value generated per professional rather than the number of employees added.The shift is already reflected in hiring patterns. An analysis of more than 5,000 live openings and over 20,000 roles hired by GCCs in the past year found that about 62% of hiring was concentrated among professionals with three to eight years of experience, with median experience at six years. GCCs are increasingly seeking professionals who can become productive quickly and bring a combination of technical and domain expertise.AI skills are also attracting a significant compensation premium. The report’s salary analysis puts annual pay for AI/ML engineers at $30,000–$50,000 at the engineer level, $45,000–$90,000 for senior professionals and $150,000–$200,000-plus for lead/principal roles.Forward-deployed engineers, who combine engineering, domain and customer-facing capabilities, command similarly high compensation, ranging from $40,000–$90,000 for engineers, $100,000–$110,000 for senior professionals and $150,000–$200,000-plus for lead/principal roles. Cloud, DevOps, SRE and platform engineering are also attracting premiums as GCCs build infrastructure for AI and data platforms.GCC hiring grew about 12–15% year-on-year in the first half of 2026, significantly faster than the broader IT/ITeS sector, according to the report. Demand for AI-related roles rose about 45% year-on-year, while nearly 65% of new positions now require AI skills.The report said GCC expansion is therefore becoming less about adding headcount and more about increasing capability density. Centres are hiring fewer but more senior and specialised professionals, while combining strategic core employees with flex talent such as contractors, specialist partners, build-operate-transfer teams and AI agents.“FY26 data is the decoupling of value growth from people growth,” the report said, adding that organisations are prioritising redeployment and AI-led productivity over linear headcount addition. “Hiring has not stopped; it has changed shape.”Get the latest Business News and Live updates. 30-year vs. 15-year fixed mortgage rates

Generally, 15-year mortgage rates are lower than those for 30-year mortgages. With a fixed-rate mortgage , your rate is locked in from day one. However, you will get a new rate if you refinance your mortgage.

An adjustable-rate mortgage keeps your rate the same for a specified period. Then, the rate will increase or decrease depending on several factors, such as the economy, and the maximum amount your rate can change according to your contract. For example, with a 7/1 ARM, your rate would be locked in for the first seven years, then adjust annually for the remainder of your term.

articles.summary: India Business News: Zetwerk and US-based Ayr Energy reach global settlement ending trade-secret disputes in Texas, Bengaluru and the ITC; all claims dismissed, terms undisclosed.
articles.body: BENGALURU: Manufacturing platform Zetwerk and US power equipment maker Ayr Energy have settled their legal disputes, ending a months-long battle in which the two sides accused each other of stealing confidential information and trade secrets.The companies said on Monday that they had reached a global settlement covering all outstanding disputes between them, their affiliates and individuals involved in the cases. They dismissed claims pending before the Texas Business Court, as well as proceedings involving Zetwerk and Ayr co-founder Anirudh Reddy in a Bengaluru court. The two sides also jointly sought termination of the related investigation before the US International Trade Commission (ITC).Financial and other terms of the settlement were not disclosed.The agreement closes a legal fight that began when Zetwerk took Ayr to court. In October 2025, Zetwerk and its US subsidiary Unimacts Global sued Ayr and Reddy in Texas, alleging that Reddy had incorporated Ayr while serving as a senior Zetwerk executive and had taken confidential customer, pricing, supply-chain and technical information with him. Zetwerk had sought around $100 million in damages.Ayr subsequently brought its own claims against Zetwerk, accusing the Indian company and its affiliates of improperly obtaining Ayr’s confidential information to build a competing transformer business in the US.Ayr had also approached the ITC, seeking restrictions on imports of transformers it alleged were linked to the misuse of its trade secrets. Its counterclaims in the Texas proceedings had sought damages of at least $1 billion. articles.title: Anyone who has used CVS’ website is owed money. Here’s how to get a payment
articles.summary: Are you a CVS customer? Or have you ever been? There’s a good chance you qualify for a payment in a $20.5 million class action settlement reached with the pharmacy chain.
articles.body:
(NEXSTAR) – Are you a CVS customer? Or have you ever been? There’s a good chance you qualify for a payment in a $20.5 million class action settlement reached with the pharmacy chain.

The class action lawsuit claims CVS disclosed customers’ personal data collected on the pharmacy’s website to Criteo, an advertising company. CVS said it hasn’t violated any laws, but agreed to settle the case.

Included in the settlement are direct payments of either $5 or $10 to affected customers – and a huge group of people are affected. “All living individuals who accessed the CVS Digital Properties in the United States prior to July 27, 2026” qualify for at least a $5 payment.

How do you know if you accessed one of the “CVS Digital Properties?” According to the settlement agreement , anyone who used the CVS website (CVS.com), the CVS Health website (CVSHealth.com) or the CVS app all qualify. That could have been to make a vaccine appointment, check on a prescription, order something online, print photos, or anything else.

The trick is that if you want the full $10 payment, you’ll have to prove you used the website or app when filing a claim. The claim form prompts you to upload a piece of proof, “like browser search history, screenshots showing dates, and/or email receipts of online purchases demonstrating your access of a CVS Digital Property prior to July 27, 2026.”

If you can’t prove you used the site or app, you can still file a claim for $5.

You can fill out the claim form online or send it by mail. The deadline to file is Nov. 16, and you can elect to receive your payment by PayPal, Venmo or Zelle.

A final approval hearing in the case is scheduled for Dec. 1.

articles.title: Should you apply for multiple credit cards at once?
articles.summary: Applying for multiple credit cards at once can affect your credit and make welcome bonuses harder to earn. Here’s what to consider before you apply.
articles.body:

In general, it's better to space out credit card applications rather than apply for multiple cards at once . Each application can result in a hard credit inquiry, and opening several new accounts in a short period can affect your credit score.

Multiple applications can also make it harder to earn credit card welcome bonuses. If each card requires you to spend thousands of dollars within the first few months, you could risk overspending or missing out on a bonus altogether.

That doesn't mean you should only have one credit card. Having multiple credit cards can be useful for maximizing rewards and increasing your available credit, as long as you can manage each account responsibly.

Applying for multiple credit cards in a short period can temporarily hurt your credit score.

Unlike some mortgage, auto, and student loan inquiries, multiple credit card applications aren't grouped together as a single inquiry for rate-shopping purposes.

Opening several cards at once can lower the average age of your credit accounts.

Multiple welcome bonuses can require significant spending within a short period, making them harder to earn without overspending.

Having multiple credit cards isn't necessarily bad for your credit if you manage them responsibly.

Should you apply for multiple credit cards at the same time?

Generally, it's better to apply for one credit card at a time and leave some time between applications. Every credit card application can result in a hard inquiry on your credit report. Opening several new accounts within a short period can also reduce the average age of your accounts.

There's another practical consideration: If you're applying for rewards cards, opening several at once could leave you juggling multiple welcome bonus spending requirements, annual fees, and payment due dates. Here's a closer look at the potential downsides.

Multiple hard inquiries can affect your credit score

"New credit" accounts for about 10% of a FICO Score. When you apply for a credit card, the issuer typically performs a hard credit inquiry, which can cause a small, temporary drop in your score.

Hard inquiries can remain on your credit report for up to two years, although FICO Scores only consider inquiries from the previous 12 months.

Unlike rate shopping for certain mortgages, auto loans, and student loans, multiple credit card applications aren't generally treated as a single inquiry. That means applying for several cards within a short period can result in several separate hard inquiries.

Opening several new credit accounts quickly can also signal greater credit risk to lenders.

New cards can reduce the average age of your accounts

Length of credit history accounts for about 15% of a FICO Score. FICO considers factors including the age of your oldest account, your newest account, and the average age of your credit accounts. Opening a new credit card can lower your average account age, and opening several at once can lower it further.

The impact depends on your overall credit profile. Someone with a long, established credit history may be affected differently than someone with a relatively short credit history.

One of the biggest reasons to open a new rewards credit card is the opportunity to earn a welcome bonus. But these offers typically require you to spend a certain amount within a limited time.

Opening several cards simultaneously may mean you need to meet multiple spending requirements at once. For example, say you open one card offering 60,000 points after you spend $4,000 in the first three months and another offering 75,000 points after you spend $4,000 in the first three months.

You'd need to charge $8,000 in three months — about $2,667 per month — to earn both bonuses.

If that amount is higher than your normal spending, chasing both bonuses could encourage you to spend more than you otherwise would. And if you don't meet a card's spending requirement by the deadline, you could miss out on its bonus entirely.

Spacing out your applications can make it easier to meet each spending requirement through purchases you would have made anyway.

How long should you wait between credit card applications?

There isn't a required waiting period between credit card applications. The right timing depends on your credit history, how recently you've applied for other credit, and the requirements of the card issuer. Some issuers also have their own application or eligibility rules that may limit how frequently you can open new cards or qualify for welcome bonuses.

If you've recently opened a credit card, waiting before submitting another application can give your credit profile time to recover from the hard inquiry and new account. It can also make it easier to finish earning one welcome bonus before taking on another spending requirement.

What happens if you apply for multiple credit cards in one day?

If you apply for multiple credit cards in one day, each application can result in a separate hard inquiry on your credit report.

Submitting the applications on the same day doesn't generally combine them into a single inquiry. And if you're approved for multiple cards, you'll also have several new accounts added to your credit history.

The exact effect on your credit score varies depending on your credit profile, so there's no set number of points you should expect your score to fall.

What should you do if your credit card application is denied?

If your credit card application is denied, consider finding out why before immediately applying for another card. Another application can result in another hard inquiry without addressing whatever caused the first issuer to reject your application.

Creditors are required to provide the principal reasons for denying your application or tell you how to obtain those reasons. Review the denial notice and your credit reports for issues that may have contributed to the decision, such as high balances or inaccurate information.

Before applying for another card, you can also check whether an issuer offers prequalification or preapproval. These tools commonly use a soft credit inquiry, which doesn't affect your credit score, although prequalifying doesn't guarantee you'll ultimately be approved.

No. Having multiple credit cards isn't inherently bad for your credit. The more important question is whether you can manage them responsibly.

Multiple credit cards can help you maximize rewards across different types of spending. For example, you might use an airline credit card for flights and travel perks while using a cash-back card for everyday expenses such as groceries and gas.

Having additional available credit can also affect your credit utilization ratio. But that benefit can disappear if having more cards causes you to take on more debt.

Multiple cards may not be a good fit if you have trouble keeping track of balances and due dates, or if having access to more credit encourages you to overspend. Credit card interest and late fees can quickly outweigh the value of any rewards you earn.

Does applying for multiple credit cards hurt your credit?

It can. Each credit card application can result in a hard inquiry, which may temporarily lower your credit score. Opening multiple accounts can also reduce the average age of your credit history.

Can you apply for two credit cards at the same time?

Yes, you can apply for two credit cards at the same time, but each application is generally evaluated separately and can result in its own hard credit inquiry. Applying for two cards also means potentially managing two new accounts and two welcome bonus requirements at once.

How many credit cards can you apply for at once?

There's no universal limit on the number of credit cards you can apply for at once. However, individual issuers may have their own application and eligibility restrictions, and applying for several cards within a short period can affect your credit.

Do multiple credit card applications count as one hard inquiry?

Generally, no. Credit card applications don't receive the same rate-shopping treatment that FICO provides for certain mortgage, auto, and student loan inquiries. Each credit card application can result in a separate hard inquiry.

There's no ideal number of credit cards for everyone. The right number is the number you can manage responsibly while paying your bills on time and avoiding unnecessary debt. Some people can benefit from having several cards for different rewards or benefits, while others may be better off with one or two.

Yes, you can sometimes have two of the same credit card. Learn when issuers allow duplicate cards, what restrictions may apply, and whether it makes sense.

articles.title: What we know — and don’t — about Paramount’s Hollywood plans
articles.summary: Paramount has cleared the final hurdle in its year-long race to take over Warner Bros. Discovery. Now comes the really hard part.
articles.body: Paramount has cleared the final hurdle in its year-long race to take over Warner Bros. Discovery. Now comes the really hard part. In the coming weeks, Paramount will take control of CNN and scores of other Warner assets like HBO, DC Comics, and the Discovery Channel. Integrating all the channels, studios and streamers will take a while. While Paramount executives have had months to think through the possibilities, the work of turning two sprawling media empires into one company is only beginning. “There’s still work to get this deal across the finish line,” Paramount CEO David Ellison told staffers in a memo, “but we’re excited to bring these two iconic companies together, as it means more opportunity for our creatives, production crews and employees across the business, and more great entertainment for audiences everywhere.” Ellison sent the memo after a coalition of state attorneys general agreed to drop their antitrust lawsuit in exchange for relatively modest concessions. Analysts have called it a massive victory for the Ellisons — David and his father, Larry, the Oracle billionaire — as they assemble a global media empire. But as Paul Nary, a Wharton professor who studies mergers and acquisitions, wrote on X, “A reminder is in order: most large media megamergers fail to live up to their promises. The harder work is still ahead.” Warner CEO David Zaslav told staff in a separate memo that the merger is expected to take effect “by early October.” Combining the streamers? Consumers won’t notice any immediate changes. But over time, Paramount will likely begin merging the Paramount+ and HBO Max streaming services. The company could also look to combine CBS News and CNN’s news operations. Paramount has long positioned the merger as a way to compete more effectively with streaming behemoths like Netflix and Disney+, which boast giant digital libraries full of attractive IP. A merged Paramount–WBD will create a single company that owns HBO Max, Discovery+, Paramount+ and Pluto TV, in addition to CNN’s All Access streaming platform. That combination would also house everything from the DC Universe, “The Sopranos” and “Harry Potter” to the “Top Gun” and “Mission: Impossible” franchises. Paramount said in March that the streamer combination “gives us a little over 200 million direct-to-consumer subscribers.” The settlement did not require Paramount to divest some of its cable assets — a concession that California Attorney General Rob Bonta, who led a 12-state coalition suing to block the merger, had previously sought. But the deal does give some shape to that vast media company, at least for the five-year commitment period. Outside media and entertainment circles, it also foreshadows changes consumers may expect on their end. Creating a studio behemoth The merger will also put two major Hollywood studios, Paramount and Warner Bros., under the same ownership. A major concern among the deal’s critics was that combining the two studios would mean one larger studio giant with fewer jobs and fewer films overall. Bonta reportedly sought to require Paramount to operate the two studios separately. However, the final deal requires Paramount to preserve both studio lots and meet minimum annual film-release targets — but it does not require the studios to operate separately. The settlement commits Paramount to a reliable stream of theatrical releases for the next five full calendar years — 30 per year in the next two years, rising to 32 per year after that. Bonta told reporters on Monday that the settlement is “the opposite” of Disney’s 2019 acquisition of 21st Century Fox, which Paramount’s critics have cited as an example of theatrical output shrinking after a mega-merger. “All the things we saw in the Disney–Fox merger — a massive decrease in film production, in film output, fewer films being made — this doesn’t just guard against that and protect against a downside,” Bonta said. “It locks in a massive upside.” After the commitment period, however, things aren’t so clear. The merged company could maintain or increase output; without these requirements, it could also reduce the number of movies released or its domestic production spending. To ensure the company honors the terms during the five-year period, the state attorneys general built two penalties for missing commitments. Paramount would have to pay $30 million per film below the annual requirement — half going to designated film-industry union health and retirement trust funds, 40% to the Motion Picture & Television Fund and 10% to a National Association of Attorneys General fund. The company would also have to divest its ownership interest in Miramax, a joint venture studio, if it fails to meet the theatrical-release quota and doesn’t make up the shortfall within six months. Paramount also agreed not to sell or close Paramount’s Hollywood studio lot or Warner’s Burbank lot during the five-year commitment period. At one point during Paramount’s tense standoff with the state attorneys general, the company threatened to move its headquarters out of Los Angeles — a threat that many viewed as an effort to twist Bonta’s arm into cutting a favorable deal. With the settlement secured, Ellison said the newly combined company will stay put. “We’re eager to get to work building a stronger Hollywood,” he wrote in a statement on Monday. “Let me be clear: the newly merged company will be headquartered in Los Angeles. We aren’t going anywhere. Our history is here and this is where our future is being built.”

articles.title: What is the prime rate, and how does it affect you?
articles.summary: What is the prime rate? And how does it impact your borrowing costs? Learn more about the interest rate that banks charge their "best" customers.
articles.body:
Some offers on this page are from advertisers who pay us, which may affect which products we write about, but not our recommendations. See our Advertiser Disclosure .

The prime rate is an important benchmark interest rate that can affect how much you pay to borrow money. Banks use the prime rate to help set rates on credit cards, home equity lines of credit (HELOCs), personal loans, and other forms of variable-rate debt.

Understanding how the prime rate works — and why it changes — can help you anticipate changes in your borrowing costs and make smarter decisions about your debt.

What is the prime rate, and how does it work?

The prime rate, also known as the Wall Street Journal prime rate or U.S. prime rate, is the interest rate at which banks lend money to their most creditworthy customers.

Individual banks set their own prime rates, and the Wall Street Journal publishes an aggregate rate set by at least 70% of the country's 10 largest banks. This Wall Street Journal prime rate provides a benchmark that banks can use to set rates on various loan products. Currently, the prime rate is 7%.

You can think of the prime rate as a reference point for consumer loan interest rates. For example, a higher prime rate means higher credit card interest rates, adjustable-rate mortgage rates, and personal loan rates. However, banks use additional factors, including the borrower's credit history, to determine individual interest rates. Generally, the better your credit, the lower your loan interest rate — and the closer your rate will be to the prime rate.

The prime rate isn't fixed; it changes in response to the federal funds rate. Typically, the prime rate is about 3 percentage points higher than the upper range of the federal funds rate. For example, if the upper end of the federal funds target range were 3.5%, the prime rate would be about 6.5%. Inflation and other economic factors can also affect the prime rate.

The prime rate fluctuates over time in response to various factors that affect the economy, including wars, recessions, and global events. It reached a high of 21.5% in 1980 due to rampant inflation. It was the lowest at 3.25% in 2008 during the Great Recession, and again in 2020 during the COVID-19 pandemic economic response. Today, the prime rate is 7%.

Here's a snapshot of the prime rate over the past 10 years:

Because banks use the prime rate as a reference point for setting interest rates, the prime rate directly influences a variety of loan interest rates, including personal loans, home equity products, mortgages, credit cards, and more.

Some loans — like certain personal loans and mortgages — have fixed rates, meaning their interest rates don't change throughout the loan's term. Others, such as credit cards, have variable rates that can change at any time.

If you have an outstanding variable-rate loan, such as a home equity line of credit (HELOC) or credit card, an increase in the prime rate can lead to a bump in your interest rate — and, therefore, a higher monthly payment. If you have an existing fixed-rate loan, a change in the prime rate won't affect your current interest rate or payments. But it will affect the rates of any new fixed-rate loans you take out.

Generally speaking, a higher prime rate leads to higher interest rates, making it more expensive to borrow. Your individual credit history also affects the interest rates you qualify for, but the prime rate acts as a starting point.
